findings: ちゃん is an affectionate/familiar suffix used with names and nicknames. No lexicographic or sociolinguistic primary source for this entry was obtained in this follow-up.
It is common for children, relatives, close friends and pets. The article’s domain/frequency list has no source locator.
It is not exclusively feminine and can be used for boys, men, pets or characters. The government report says honorific/affectionate forms depend on style and context but does not analyze ちゃん.
Age, intimacy, hierarchy and group convention determine appropriateness. The report supports contextual variation generally, not the specific ちゃん judgments or examples.
